papers.title: Porosity Measurement for HIPped AM Ti6Al4V Samples – A Practical Comparison between Archimedes Method and Micro-CT
papers.abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of porosity measurement techniques using the Archimedes method and micro-computed tomography (Micro-CT) for additively manufactured (AM) Ti-6Al-4V components. The samples were subjected to four different post-processing conditions: three groups were processed using Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) with varying parameters, while one group remained in the as-built condition. A total of 16 samples were analyzed, with each group comprising four specimens. To enhance the mechanical performance of AM parts, particularly their fatigue strength, maximizing relative density (approaching 100%) and optimizing the morphology of the defects are primary objectives. Among post-processing techniques, HIP is one of the most effective methods for reducing or eliminating internal porosity, thereby increasing the overall density of as-built materials, which typically exhibit densities exceeding 99% of the theoretical value. The presence, morphology, and distribution of porosity are especially critical in determining fatigue behavior. The experimental setup included: Group 1: HIP at 920 °C, 100 MPa, for 2 hours, Group 2: HIP at 815 °C, 190 MPa, for 2 hours, Group 3: HIP at 920 °C, 100 MPa, for 2 hours with uniform rapid quenching, and Group 4: As-built condition (no post-processing) Density measurements were performed on all samples using the Archimedes method. Additionally, one representative sample from each group was partially scanned using Micro-CT to evaluate internal porosity characteristics. A comparative analysis of the results from both techniques revealed a consistent correlation between them. While the Archimedes method offers a faster, more cost-effective approach for quantifying overall porosity levels, Micro-CT provides valuable insights into the spatial distribution, size, and morphology of pores within the material—information that cannot be captured through the Archimedes technique alone.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文比较了热等静压后Ti6Al4V增材制造样品的孔隙率测量方法，虽未直接测试力学性能，但对评估后处理效果有参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not directly measure mechanical performance (fatigue, tensile) or microstructure evolution; it focuses on comparing porosity measurement techniques.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较热等静压后Ti6Al4V样品孔隙率测量方法的准确性。
summary_zh.method: 采用阿基米德法和微CT对四种后处理状态的样品进行孔隙率测量并对比。
summary_zh.result: 两种方法结果一致，但微CT可提供孔隙空间分布和形态信息。
summary_zh.validation: 通过16个样品分组实验进行对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To compare porosity measurement techniques for hot isostatic pressed (HIP) additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V samples.
summary_en.method: Archimedes method and micro-CT were used to measure porosity of samples in four groups: three HIP conditions and one as-built.
summary_en.result: Good correlation between methods was found, with micro-CT providing additional spatial distribution and morphology of pores.
summary_en.validation: Experimental comparison using 16 samples with partial micro-CT scans.
